title: Introduction to Grammar
description: Fundamental concepts for Japanese sentence structure.

points.usage: Basic sentence structure. 'wa' marks the topic.
points.example:
私は学生です。
(Watashi wa gakusei desu.)
I am a student.

points.pattern: AはBではありません (A wa B dewa arimasen)
points.usage: Negative form of 'desu'.
points.example:
これは本ではありません。
(Kore wa hon dewa arimasen.)
This is not a book.

points.pattern: AはBですか (A wa B desu ka)
points.usage: Question form. 'ka' makes it a question.
points.example:
あなたは日本人ですか。
(Anata wa Nihonjin desu ka.)
Are you Japanese?

title: Essential Particles
description: Crucial markers that define word relationships.

points.usage: Marks the direct object of an action.
points.example:
水を飲みます。
(Mizu o nomimasu.)
I drink water.

points.usage: Marks destination, specific time, or location of existence.
points.example:
学校に行きます。
(Gakkou ni ikimasu.)
I go to school.

points.usage: Marks where an action happens or the tool used.
points.example:
バスで帰ります。
(Basu de kaerimasu.)
I go home by bus.

points.usage: Connects nouns or indicates accompaniment.
points.example:
友達と話します。
(Tomodachi to hanashimasu.)
I talk with a friend.

title: Verb Te-form (て形)
description: A versatile verb form used for requests and connecting actions.

points.usage: Polite request.
points.example:
見てください。
(Mite kudasai.)
Please look.

points.usage: Ongoing action or state.
points.example:
雨が降っています。
(Ame ga futte imasu.)
It is raining.

points.pattern: 〜てもいいですか (~te mo ii desu ka)
points.usage: Asking for permission.
points.example:
写真を撮ってもいいですか。
(Shashin o totte mo ii desu ka.)
May I take a photo?

points.usage: Prohibition.
points.example:
ここに入ってはいけません。
(Koko ni haitte wa ikemasen.)
You must not enter here.

title: Verb Nai-form (ない形)
description: Negative verb form used in various grammar patterns.

points.usage: Polite negative request.
points.example:
行かないでください。
(Ikanaide kudasai.)
Please don't go.

points.usage: Obligation.
points.example:
勉強しなければなりません。
(Benkyou shinakereba narimasen.)
I must study.

points.pattern: 〜なくてもいいです (~nakutemo ii desu)
points.usage: Lack of obligation.
points.example:
明日来なくてもいいです。
(Ashita konakutemo ii desu.)
You don't have to come tomorrow.

title: Verb Ta-form (た形)
description: Past tense form used for experience and listing actions.

points.pattern: 〜たことがある (~ta koto ga aru)
points.usage: Past experience.
points.example:
日本に行ったことがあります。
(Nihon ni itta koto ga arimasu.)
I have been to Japan.

points.usage: Listing representative actions.
points.example:
本を読んだり、テレビを見たりします。
(Hon o yondari, terebi o mitari shimasu.)
I read books, watch TV, etc.

title: Adjective Conjugations
description: How to modify and connect adjectives.

points.usage: Connecting sentences with i-adjectives.
points.example:
この本は安くて面白いです。
(Kono hon wa yasukute omoshiroi desu.)
This book is cheap and interesting.

points.usage: Connecting sentences with na-adjectives.
points.example:
彼は親切で元気です。
(Kare wa shinsetsu de genki desu.)
He is kind and energetic.

title: Conditional Forms (条件形)
description: Various ways to express 'if' and conditional relationships in Japanese.

points.usage: General conditional. Used for both hypothetical and temporal conditions.
points.example:
雨が降ったら、家にいます。
(Ame ga futtara, ie ni imasu.)
If it rains, I will stay home.

points.usage: Hypothetical conditional emphasizing the condition itself. Often used for general truths.
points.example:
安ければ、買います。
(Yasukereba, kaimasu.)
If it's cheap, I'll buy it.

points.usage: Contextual conditional. Used when reacting to new information or a topic raised by someone.
points.example:
日本に行くなら、京都がおすすめです。
(Nihon ni iku nara, Kyouto ga osusume desu.)
If you're going to Japan, I recommend Kyoto.

points.usage: Expresses automatic or habitual results. Used for natural consequences and instructions.
points.example:
春になると、桜が咲きます。
(Haru ni naru to, sakura ga sakimasu.)
Whenever spring comes, the cherry blossoms bloom.

title: Passive & Causative (受身・使役)
description: Forms for expressing passive actions, causation, and forced actions.

points.usage: Passive voice. The subject receives the action. Often implies inconvenience in Japanese.
points.example:
弟にケーキを食べられました。
(Otouto ni keeki o taberaremashita.)
My cake was eaten by my younger brother.

points.usage: Causative form. Indicates making or allowing someone to perform an action.
points.example:
母は子供に野菜を食べさせました。
(Haha wa kodomo ni yasai o tabesasemashita.)
The mother made the child eat vegetables.

points.usage: Combines causative and passive. The subject is forced to do something against their will.
points.example:
毎日残業させられています。
(Mainichi zangyou saserarete imasu.)
I am made to work overtime every day.

points.usage: Potential form. Expresses ability or possibility. Ichidan verbs add -られる, godan verbs change the ending.
points.example:
漢字が読めますか。
(Kanji ga yomemasu ka.)
Can you read kanji?

points.usage: Volitional form. Expresses intention or suggests doing something together.
points.example:
明日早く起きよう。
(Ashita hayaku okiyou.)
Let's wake up early tomorrow.

points.usage: Expresses a plan or intention that has already been decided.
points.example:
来年日本に留学するつもりです。
(Rainen Nihon ni ryuugaku suru tsumori desu.)
I intend to study abroad in Japan next year.

points.usage: Expresses a decision made by the speaker. Emphasizes the act of deciding.
points.example:
毎朝ジョギングすることにしました。
(Maiasa jogingu suru koto ni shimashita.)
I decided to jog every morning.

title: Giving & Receiving (授受)
description: Expressions for giving and receiving actions, reflecting social relationships.

points.usage: The speaker (or in-group) does a favor for someone else. Can sound condescending if used carelessly.
points.example:
友達に日本語を教えてあげました。
(Tomodachi ni Nihongo o oshiete agemashita.)
I taught Japanese to my friend (as a favor).

points.usage: The speaker receives a favor from someone. Implies gratitude.
points.example:
先生に作文を直してもらいました。
(Sensei ni sakubun o naoshite moraimashita.)
I had my teacher correct my essay.

points.usage: Someone does a favor for the speaker (or in-group). Expresses appreciation.
points.example:
母が弁当を作ってくれました。
(Haha ga bentou o tsukutte kuremashita.)
My mother made a bento for me.

title: Hearsay & Appearance (伝聞・様態)
description: Ways to express what something looks like, what you heard, and what seems to be the case.

points.usage: Describes appearance based on direct observation. Attaches to verb stems or adjective stems.
points.example:
このケーキはおいしそうです。
(Kono keeki wa oishisou desu.)
This cake looks delicious.

points.usage: Reports information heard from another source. Attaches to the plain form of verbs and adjectives.
points.example:
明日は雨だそうです。
(Ashita wa ame da sou desu.)
I heard that it will rain tomorrow.

points.usage: Expresses conjecture based on evidence. みたいだ is more casual than ようだ.
points.example:
彼は忙しいようです。
(Kare wa isogashii you desu.)
It seems like he is busy.

points.usage: Expresses inference based on indirect evidence or hearsay. Less certain than ようだ.
points.example:
新しいレストランはおいしいらしいです。
(Atarashii resutoran wa oishii rashii desu.)
Apparently the new restaurant is good.

title: Conjunctions & Connectors
description: Patterns for connecting clauses and expressing contrast, concession, and addition.

points.usage: Expresses that the result holds true regardless of the condition.
points.example:
雨が降っても、サッカーをします。
(Ame ga futte mo, sakkaa o shimasu.)
Even if it rains, I will play soccer.

points.usage: Expresses unexpected contrast or disappointment about a result.
points.example:
たくさん勉強したのに、試験に落ちました。
(Takusan benkyou shita noni, shiken ni ochimashita.)
Despite studying a lot, I failed the exam.

points.usage: Expresses two simultaneous actions performed by the same subject.
points.example:
音楽を聞きながら、料理をします。
(Ongaku o kikinagara, ryouri o shimasu.)
I cook while listening to music.

points.usage: Lists multiple reasons or qualities. Often used to justify a conclusion.
points.example:
この店は安いし、おいしいし、最高です。
(Kono mise wa yasui shi, oishii shi, saikou desu.)
This restaurant is cheap, delicious, and the best.

title: Key Expressions (重要表現)
description: Important intermediate expressions for describing habits, changes, and recent events.

points.usage: Describes something that happens occasionally. Uses the dictionary form of the verb.
points.example:
朝ごはんを食べないことがあります。
(Asagohan o tabenai koto ga arimasu.)
There are times when I don't eat breakfast.

points.meaning: Try to / Make an effort to
points.usage: Expresses a conscious effort to do or avoid something.
points.example:
毎日運動するようにしています。
(Mainichi undou suru you ni shite imasu.)
I try to exercise every day.

points.usage: Expresses a gradual change in ability or state over time.
points.example:
日本語が話せるようになりました。
(Nihongo ga hanaseru you ni narimashita.)
I became able to speak Japanese.

points.pattern: 〜ことにしている (~koto ni shite iru)
points.meaning: Make it a rule to / Habitually
points.usage: Describes a personal rule or habit that one has decided to maintain.
points.example:
寝る前に本を読むことにしています。
(Neru mae ni hon o yomu koto ni shite imasu.)
I make it a rule to read before bed.

points.usage: Indicates that an action was just completed recently, or that someone does nothing but one thing.
points.example:
今昼ごはんを食べたばかりです。
(Ima hirugohan o tabeta bakari desu.)
I just ate lunch.

title: Formal Patterns (敬語表現)
description: Honorific and humble expressions used in formal and business contexts.

points.usage: Humble form of てもらう. Used in formal situations to express receiving a favor.
points.example:
先生に推薦状を書いていただきました。
(Sensei ni suisenjou o kaite itadakimashita.)
I humbly had my teacher write a recommendation letter.

points.usage: Polite form of あります/です. Used in formal speech and customer service.
points.example:
お手洗いは二階でございます。
(Otearai wa nikai de gozaimasu.)
The restroom is on the second floor.

points.usage: Humble form of ていきます. Used to humbly describe one's own actions in formal settings.
points.example:
努力してまいります。
(Doryoku shite mairimasu.)
I will continue to make efforts (humble).

points.pattern: おVになる (o V ni naru)
points.usage: Honorific pattern to elevate the actions of the person you are speaking about.
points.example:
先生はもうお帰りになりました。
(Sensei wa mou okaeri ni narimashita.)
The teacher has already left (honorific).

title: Reasoning & Cause (理由・原因)
description: Patterns for expressing logical conclusions, expectations, and reasoning.

points.usage: Indicates a logical conclusion drawn from known facts or circumstances.
points.example:
毎日練習しているから、上手なわけだ。
(Mainichi renshuu shite iru kara, jouzu na wake da.)
He practices every day, so no wonder he's good.

points.usage: Expresses an expectation based on logic or evidence. Implies confidence in the conclusion.
points.example:
彼はもう着いたはずです。
(Kare wa mou tsuita hazu desu.)
He should have arrived by now.

points.usage: Strongly denies a possibility based on logical reasoning.
points.example:
彼がそんなことを言うわけがない。
(Kare ga sonna koto o iu wake ga nai.)
There's no way he would say such a thing.

points.usage: Expresses strong certainty or conviction about something.
points.example:
あの音は雷に違いない。
(Ano oto wa kaminari ni chigai nai.)
That sound must be thunder.

points.meaning: It's not that / It doesn't mean that
points.usage: Partially denies something. Clarifies that a general assumption is not entirely true.
points.example:
嫌いなわけではないが、あまり食べません。
(Kirai na wake dewa nai ga, amari tabemasen.)
It's not that I dislike it, but I don't eat it much.

title: Comparison & Degree (比較・程度)
description: Patterns for expressing extent, proportional relationships, and emphasis.

points.usage: Expresses the degree or extent of something. Often used for emphasis or comparison.
points.example:
泣きたいほど嬉しかったです。
(Nakitai hodo ureshikatta desu.)
I was so happy I could cry.

points.usage: Expresses a proportional relationship between two things.
points.example:
練習すればするほど上手になります。
(Renshuu sureba suru hodo jouzu ni narimasu.)
The more you practice, the better you get.

points.usage: Indicates an approximate degree or amount. Can also express a minimal expectation.
points.example:
自分の名前くらい漢字で書けます。
(Jibun no namae kurai kanji de kakemasu.)
I can at least write my own name in kanji.

points.usage: Emphasizes a single sufficient condition for a result.
points.example:
薬を飲みさえすれば、治ります。
(Kusuri o nomi sae sureba, naorimasu.)
If you just take the medicine, you'll get better.

points.usage: Adds strong emphasis to the preceding word, highlighting it as the most important element.
points.example:
今年こそ日本語能力試験に合格したい。
(Kotoshi koso Nihongo nouryoku shiken ni goukaku shitai.)
This year, for sure, I want to pass the JLPT.

title: Complex Sentences (複文)
description: Patterns for constructing complex sentences with purpose, contrast, and topic reference.

points.usage: Expresses purpose (with volitional verbs) or cause (with non-volitional verbs/nouns).
points.example:
留学するために、お金を貯めています。
(Ryuugaku suru tame ni, okane o tamete imasu.)
I am saving money in order to study abroad.

points.meaning: So that / In such a way that
points.usage: Expresses a desired outcome or goal. Used with non-volitional verbs or potential forms.
points.example:
忘れないように、メモを取りました。
(Wasurenai you ni, memo o torimashita.)
I took notes so that I wouldn't forget.

points.usage: Indicates a role, capacity, or status in which someone or something acts.
points.example:
彼は医者として働いています。
(Kare wa isha to shite hataraite imasu.)
He works as a doctor.

points.usage: Indicates the target of an action or feeling, or draws a contrast between two things.
points.example:
兄はスポーツが好きなのに対して、弟は読書が好きです。
(Ani wa supootsu ga suki na noni taishite, otouto wa dokusho ga suki desu.)
While the older brother likes sports, the younger brother likes reading.

points.usage: Indicates the topic or subject being discussed or investigated.
points.example:
日本の文化について研究しています。
(Nihon no bunka ni tsuite kenkyuu shite imasu.)
I am researching about Japanese culture.

title: Change & State (変化・状態)
description: Patterns for expressing ongoing states, habits, and degrees of completion.

points.pattern: 〜ようにしている (~you ni shite iru)
points.meaning: Make a habit of / Try to regularly
points.usage: Describes an ongoing effort or habit that one consciously maintains.
points.example:
野菜を多く食べるようにしています。
(Yasai o ooku taberu you ni shite imasu.)
I make a habit of eating lots of vegetables.

points.meaning: Left in a state / Keep doing
points.usage: Indicates something is left in an undesirable state, or an action continues without stopping.
points.example:
エアコンをつけっぱなしで寝てしまいました。
(Eakon o tsukeppanashi de nete shimaimashita.)
I fell asleep with the air conditioner left on.

points.meaning: In the state of / As it is
points.usage: Describes a state that remains unchanged, often implying it should have been changed.
points.example:
靴を履いたまま家に入らないでください。
(Kutsu o haita mama ie ni hairanaide kudasai.)
Please don't enter the house with your shoes on.

points.meaning: Completely do / Do to the end
points.usage: Expresses completing an action fully or doing something to its limit.
points.example:
マラソンを走りきりました。
(Marason o hashirikirimashita.)
I ran the entire marathon to the end.

points.usage: Indicates that an action has started but is not yet finished, or is on the verge of happening.
points.example:
読みかけの本がたくさんあります。
(Yomikake no hon ga takusan arimasu.)
I have many half-read books.
